risk_description: A required project drawing or instruction is not issued when needed, creating a risk that the affected work will be delayed or disrupted.
The contractor cannot obtain timely access to a required part of the construction site, preventing planned work from proceeding.
Important information about site conditions available to the employer has not been provided to the contractor, creating uncertainty for the works.
The contractor is not fulfilling its overall contractual obligations or is failing to provide the personnel, equipment, materials, or services needed to execute the works.
The contractor has not provided the required security for proper performance of its contractual obligations.
Unexpected ground or subsurface conditions are encountered during the works, causing unforeseen difficulties and potentially increasing the work required, cost, or completion time.
Construction activities are creating pollution or other environmental impacts that require additional controls to protect the environment.
Workers on the project are exposed to unsafe conditions or inadequate health and safety arrangements, creating a risk of injury or illness.
Construction work is being carried out without the required standard of care, proper workmanship, or compliance with the specified method of execution.
The quality of materials, plant, or workmanship needs to be examined or tested to verify that the completed work meets the required standards.
The contractor must carry out specified tests on the works but may fail to provide the necessary testing equipment, staff, or arrangements.
A known or foreseeable event may interfere with construction performance and could increase costs or delay completion if it is not addressed early.
Progress of the works is being affected and the planned completion date may need to be extended because of a qualifying delay.
The contractor is experiencing disruption that is affecting progress and may prevent the works from being completed within the required time.
Construction activities have been suspended or interrupted, creating a risk of further delay to completion.
The works are ready to be taken over, but the process of obtaining completion and possession is affecting the planned project schedule.
Defects or other non-conforming work remain in the completed works and must be corrected before the required quality can be achieved.
Work, materials, or workmanship do not comply with the contract and must be remedied, potentially creating additional corrective work.
A change in legislation or regulatory requirements increases the cost of carrying out the contracted works.
The contractor requires the agreed advance payment to support the financial requirements of carrying out the project.
The contractor submits a payment application for amounts it believes are currently due under the contract.
An interim payment certificate is delayed or cannot be issued because the contractual conditions for payment have not been satisfied.
A payment due under the contract is not made within the required period, creating a financial impact on the project.
The contractor is considering suspending the works because the employer has failed to make a required payment or maintain the necessary financial arrangements.
Responsibility for loss, damage, or other contractual consequences arising during execution of the works needs to be determined between the parties.
The contractor has caused loss or damage through its actions or failure to meet its contractual responsibilities.
The employer's use of project documents or other protected material creates a risk of an intellectual property or third-party rights issue.
An extraordinary event outside the parties' reasonable control has occurred and may prevent normal contractual performance.
An extraordinary event has occurred and the affected party needs to formally notify the other party of the event and its effects.
An exceptional event is disrupting the works, and reasonable measures are needed to minimise the resulting delay.
An exceptional event is preventing normal performance and may give rise to additional cost, delay, or an extension of time.
An exceptional event continues to prevent performance of the contract, creating a potential need to terminate the contract.
The parties need to address the contractual consequences of an exceptional event affecting continued performance of the works.
The project requires appropriate insurance arrangements to cover specified risks and protect the parties against insured losses.
A contractor believes that an event or circumstance has created an entitlement to additional payment, an extension of time, or another contractual remedy and intends to submit a claim.
A contractor needs to comply with the contractual procedure and deadlines for submitting and supporting a claim for additional entitlement.
The parties disagree about a contractual matter and need an independent dispute-resolution mechanism to determine the disagreement.
The parties have failed to appoint the required dispute-board member, creating a procedural problem in the dispute-resolution process.
A contractual disagreement has not been resolved between the parties and needs to be referred through the agreed dispute-resolution procedure.
A dispute remains unresolved and may need to proceed to the next formal stage of contractual dispute resolution.
